c: , along with Ararat and Ashkenaz, as aggressors against Babylon. The Minni first appear in Assyrian inscriptions during the reign of Shalmaneser III (858–824

), who pillaged and subdued the people. They lived between Lake Urmia and Lake Van, north of Babylon, and are identified with the Mannean people, regularly associated with Urarteans (Ararat) in Assyrian manuscripts. The Minni were restless subjects. They revolted against Assyria in 716 and 715
. Further agitation occurred in the reign of Ashurbanipal (669–627
). After Nineveh’s fall to the Babylonians in 612
, the Minni disappear from the extrabiblical record.
